title: A 900-Year-Old Village Built in the Shape of an Ox — Anhui's Hongcun | China Travel Expert
description:
A whole village, laid out in the shape of an ox — and it was planned that way over 900 years ago.

Hongcun, in Yi County near Huangshan in southern Anhui, was founded in 1131 during the Southern Song dynasty. Its layout mimics an ox: a hill is the head, two old trees the horns, the winding stream the "intestines," and the crescent Moon Pond at the center the "stomach." That ingenious water system carries fresh water to every doorstep and stores it for fire emergencies. 138 Ming and Qing houses still stand, which is why it's called "the village in a Chinese painting." It was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2000.

🧭 Expert Tip: Arrive at dawn. Moon Pond turns into a perfect mirror of the whole village before the tour groups show up — the best reflection photo of your trip.
